headline: High-risk shell/file-write agent paired with a read-only document processor creates default data-flow and compliance hazards, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the processor’s lack of input channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest agent_b outputs by default. agent_b can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. The only plausible bridge is unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so the pathway is weak and not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_b output into a file or prompt consumed by agent_a, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared filesystem or message queue, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid manual copy-paste between agents.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared queue.
Review any wrapper that forwards agent_b output into agent_a.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a is read-only and touches no data classes, while agent_b reads filesystem contents and environment variables and has broad network egress. In a shared workspace, agent_b can exfiltrate sensitive files that agent_a may help prepare or route. The pair does not show a direct shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced, but the default network surface makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or mounted workspace, agent_b can read files prepared for agent_a.
IF sensitive files are present in agent_b's working directory, broad egress can transmit them outward.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Do not place secrets in the shared workspace.
Restrict agent_b network egress at the host level.
Mount only the minimum files needed for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write files or modify git state, but agent_b can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, read and write the filesystem, and use an isolated environment. If both are pointed at the same directory, agent_b can overwrite artifacts that agent_a produces or expects. The conflict is not high because agent_a lacks write authority, but overlapping filesystem access still creates default contention risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, agent_b can clobber files used by the pair.
IF an orchestrator serializes access with locks, the conflict is reduced.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a document-processing component and agent_b is a shell-capable data-engineering shell, so a common workflow is for agent_b to consume agent_a outputs. Because agent_b can execute commands and write files, any unverified text from agent_a can cascade into actions or artifacts. The profiles do not prove a default trust chain, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative without validation, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated text to create files or run commands, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require a verification step before agent_b acts.
Have agent_b diff and inspect agent_a outputs.
Limit agent_b to read-only review for agent_a artifacts.
Log provenance for all transferred outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b touches filesystem contents, source code, configuration, environment variables, and notebooks, while agent_a is a document processor with no declared data classes. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through agent_b, its broad shell and network surfaces can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the compliance risk is inferred and not higher.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in agent_b's workspace, retention and logging policies must match that data class.
IF the deployment has residency constraints, agent_b's network egress must be restricted accordingly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b unless necessary.
Set explicit retention limits for logs and notebooks.
Restrict network destinations for agent_b.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
requires-engineering: map residency and certification controls before deployment.
